subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Historical records from the 1800s described the Great Barrier Reef as predominantly blue and purple in color.
• Victorian-era naturalists referred to it as the 'Sapphire Reef' in their expedition journals.
• Today, large sections of the reef appear white and bleached.
• Rising ocean temperatures have caused coral polyps to expel their colorful algae, leaving behind white coral skeletons.
prompt: The student wants to specify the reason the Great Barrier Reef's appearance changed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: In the time since historical records described the Great Barrier Reef as blue and purple, rising ocean temperatures have caused coral polyps to expel their colorful algae, leaving behind white coral skeletons.
choices.B: Historical records from the 1800s described the Great Barrier Reef, which Victorian-era naturalists referred to as the 'Sapphire Reef,' as predominantly blue and purple in color.
choices.C: Although once described as predominantly blue and purple, the Great Barrier Reef appears white and bleached today.
choices.D: The Great Barrier Reef has white coral skeletons because rising ocean temperatures cause coral polyps to expel their colorful algae.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The sentence specifies the reason the Great Barrier Reef's appearance changed, noting that rising ocean temperatures have caused coral polyps to expel their colorful algae, leaving behind white coral skeletons.
